AWPTCM-T33369.objective:
• When two-step authentication is enabled with MAC as the first method and 802.1X as the second method, a correct MAC address at the first step transitions the supplicant to the "Connecting" state awaiting the second-step 802.1X authentication.
  • Invalid MAC at the first step places the supplicant in the HELD state for the duration of the quiet-period.
  • Invalid credentials at the second-step 802.1X authentication place the supplicant in the HELD state for the quiet-period.
  • Successful completion of the second-step 802.1X authentication results in the supplicant reaching the Authenticated state.
  • Correct log messages are generated at the appropriate times for success and failure of each step (first MAC and second 802.1X).
  • The "auth two-step enable" command is accepted, appears in running-config, persists after save and reboot, and can be disabled with the "no" form.
  • The "show auth two-step supplicant" (and brief) commands accurately report two-step information including firstMethod (mac), secondMethod (802.1x), per-supplicant status for each step, and counts.
  • The maximum number of supplicants supported for two-step auth (1st MAC / 2nd 802.1X) is correctly enforced.
  • Repeated execution of two-step authentication using 1st MAC / 2nd 802.1X does not cause crashes, hangs, or errors.
  • MAC-based and 802.1X authentication can operate together (including in two-step mode) without interference on supported ports.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability. Primary coverage from TestLink two-step family (AWP-14782 primary 1st MAC/2nd 802.1x + AWP-14773 enable, AWP-14774 show, AWP-14776/14779 logs, AWP-14879 max supplicants, AWP-14882 repeat, AWP-6858 simultaneous). ART coverage: 6201.1033.1-5 (two-step MAC list allow/deny, MAC RADIUS, list+RADIUS, fail checks) + 1348 port auth MAC+dot1x coexistence.

Enable two-step authentication (auth two-step enable) together with MAC auth and 802.1X. Configure a port for the combination. Verify the enable command and "no" form work, persist after reboot, and appear correctly in running-config.

Connect a supplicant. Perform Two-Step with 1st step MAC (correct MAC) followed by 2nd step 802.1X (correct credentials). Verify transition through Connecting state to final Authenticated state. Confirm "show auth two-step supplicant" reports firstMethod=mac, secondMethod=802.1x (or dot1x), and step statuses.
Test failure paths: invalid MAC at 1st step (expect HELD + quiet-period), correct MAC then invalid 802.1X at 2nd step (expect HELD). Verify logs are generated at the correct steps.
Verify correct success and failure log messages are produced for each step (MAC first and 802.1X second).
Test the supported maximum number of supplicants for this two-step combination. Confirm enforcement and that excess attempts are handled correctly.
Repeat the full 1st-MAC / 2nd-802.1X two-step sequence multiple times. Confirm no crashes, hangs, or unexpected errors occur.
Confirm MAC auth list (allow/deny) and RADIUS integration work in the two-step context where supported.
